item.title: ‘Urinetown’ opens Feb. 19 at Wilkes University
item.description: “We have petticoats and corsets and cages,” cast member Cally Williams said, describing the steampunk-style costumes that lend both Victorian and futuristic vibes to Wilkes University’s production of “Urinetown.”

item.title: Campaign hands out roses to spread awareness of Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit
item.description: The Pennsylvania Policy Center and the Pennsylvanians Together campaign gave out roses at the Burnt Norton on Valentine’s Day to spread awareness about the new Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit (WPTC).

item.title: Wall Street steadies after its AI-induced sell-off
item.description: NEW YORK — U.S. stocks steadied on Friday after an encouraging update on inflation helped calm a Wall Street that’s been wracked by worries about how artificial-intelligence technology may upend the business world.

item.title: WVC girls have several district title contenders in basketball
item.description: Wyoming Valley Conference girls basketball has won a District 2 championship every year since 2015. That trend is likely continue as the tournaments begin this week.

item.title: Local real estate taxes increasing in 29 of Luzerne County’s 76 municipalities
item.description: Local real estate taxes are increasing in 29 of Luzerne County’s 76 municipalities this year, according to a county report.

item.title: H.S. Boys Basketball: WVC seeks better results in district playoffs
item.description: Wyoming Valley Conference boys basketball doesn’t want a repeat of last year at Mohegan Arena. Five championship games and no championships.

item.title: H.S. Boys Basketball: Dallas tops Crestwood for WVC title threepeat
item.description: HAZLE TWP. — When the time came to come up big, Dallas did so like the two-time defending Wyoming Valley Conference Tournament boys champion.

item.title: H.S. Girls Basketball: Hazleton Area holds off Crestwood for WVC title
item.description: HAZLE TWP. — It was just two weeks ago that Crestwood traveled down to Hazleton Area and handed the Cougars their first and only loss against a District 2 opponent this season.

item.title: Tell Giselle: When truth changes everything
item.description: Several conversations with a senior, who is preparing for their final stretch of life, brought up a number of what I call “big ticket” items. This person said they suddenly — though it likely was more than a year in the works — realized they no longer believed in the religious teachings they had taken to heart from childhood.
